provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Under D4, a rotation by an odd number of quarter turns makes the colour-2 walls horizontal. Row reversal alone keeps them vertical. The factory therefore fixes one orientation flag and the colour constants palette[0], palette[2] and palette[4]. The emitted program works directly in visible coordinates. It finds each wall as a 4-connected component of the wall colour, and the wall's axis is the median across-wall coordinate. It splits the shape colour into 8-connected components, matching the generator's diagonally connected sprites. Each component goes to the wall it touches 4-adjacently, with fallback ranking by overlap with the wall's span and then by distance. In the generator, the marker is one pixel of the true mirrored sprite. So each wall's marker is the non-background, non-wall, non-shape cell that lands exactly on the reflection of that wall's shape. Greedy nearest-Chebyshev matching is used only as a fallback. The program then paints the reflection across the wall's own column (vertical) or row (horizontal) in the marker's colour. Markers are never erased, because the generator keeps them as part of the mirrored image.
draft_notes.limitations: Assumes the constructor's domain: straight walls, one sprite per wall lying within the wall's span, one marker per wall lying on the mirror image, and non-touching rectangles. The archived rule text says the marker is 'covered or removed'. In the generator it is always covered, because it is a pixel of the reflected sprite, so no separate erase step is emitted. The archived solver's Chebyshev marker pairing is a heuristic that could mis-pair markers in fresh scenes. It is replaced by the exact mirror-membership test and kept only as a fallback. No tests were run.
